exercise.name: Band Face Pull
aliases: Band face pull with external rotation

reference.title: Band Face Pull
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read)

secondaryBodyParts: Upper back (middle and lower trapezius, rhomboids)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull to the face, breathe in as the arms go back out.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s pull, short hold, about 2 s back

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (clinical opinion); often used as a warm-up or shoulder-health accessory
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: light enough to finish with the hands beside the ears and the elbows high
prescription.progression: More reps, a longer hold, a step further back from the rack, or a stronger band

cues.text: Loop the band round a rack upright at about face height. Face it, feet hip width, a strand in each hand, overhand, arms reaching toward the upright.
Breathe out and pull the hands toward the face, elbows high and wide, about level with the shoulders.
Finish with the hands beside the ears and the knuckles turned up and back; squeeze the shoulder blades together, shoulders down.
Breathe in and let the arms go back out slowly toward the upright, keeping the band tight.
Brief pause with the arms long, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows dropping toward the ribs (turning it into a low row)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows at about shoulder height and out to the sides.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to finish the pull
mistakes.fix: Stand tall over the feet; use a lighter band or step closer to the rack.
Keep the shoulders down while the hands come back.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping the turn-out at the end
mistakes.fix: Finish with the forearms pointing up and the hands beside the ears.

kinematics.norm: Elbows at about shoulder height at the finish (clinical opinion; the face pull is a high, wide pull)
From the arms reaching forward to the upper arms in line with the shoulders or a little behind; prone horizontal abduction reached about 87% MVIC in the posterior deltoid (Reinold 2007)
The shoulders turn out at the end so the forearms point up (clinical opinion); external rotation work loads the infraspinatus (Sung 2023 compared positions and abduction angles)
From nearly straight to about 90 degrees or a little more at the finish (clinical opinion)
Elastic tension rises as the band stretches, so the load is highest at the finish; at matched effort elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar activity in shoulder exercises (Andersen 2010)
About 1 s pull, 2 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #7013, Band Face Pull, video (movement reference)
Reinold et al. 2007, electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)
Sung, Jung, Wang and Kim 2023, the effects of body positions and abduction angles on shoulder muscle activity patterns during external rotation exercises (Healthcare 11(14):1977)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
Check the band for nicks or tears and loop it securely round the upright; a band that slips or snaps can hit the face.
Band tension is user-chosen: pick one you can pull to the face with the elbows high.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort at the turn-out: finish with the hands at chin height and less rotation.
Neck tension: anchor the band a little lower, at chest height.
regressions: Lighter band or a step closer to the rack.
Band standing rear delt row (no turn-out).
progressions: Stronger band or a step further back.
Cable face pull with a rope.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back and out (horizontal abduction). Prone horizontal abduction reached about 87% MVIC in the posterior deltoid (Reinold 2007).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the finish; in prone retraction exercises the middle trapezius reached up to about 77% of maximal activity with the arms raised (Oyama 2010).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Turns the shoulder out at the end so the forearms point up; external rotation work loads it (Sung 2023).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the elbows up at shoulder height.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbows as the hands come to the face.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder blade; shrugging shifts work here.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright so the body does not lean back.
